# 1 Clement Chapter 50 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 50

---

## Council Notes

**On "splendor" / "brightness" / "radiant" (v.2):** EMET: "splendor." LOGOS: "brightness." PNEUMA: "radiant." The Greek *lampros* means bright, shining, brilliant. "Brightness in righteousness" (LOGOS) is retained as most precise and natural.

**On "boldness of speech" / "confidence" (v.2):** EMET: "truth in boldness of speech." LOGOS: "truth in confidence." The Greek *parrēsia* is the technical term for freedom of speech, boldness before God and humans. "Truth in boldness of speech" is more distinctive and preserves this important early Christian term.

**On Psalm 50/51 LXX citation (vv.7–12):** Clement quotes LXX Psalm 49 (Ps 50 MT). The citation is a sustained quotation, one of the longest in the letter. All agents render it adequately; LOGOS is the most precise. Key word: v.9 "spread slander" — EMET says "spread slander" from *dieballe*, LOGOS says "stumbling-block" (different Greek word reading). EMET reading preferred.

**On "sacrifice of praise" (v.12):** All agents agree. This is the key reversal: the psalm condemns ritual without morality, then affirms authentic sacrifice. "Sacrifice of praise" (all agents) is correct.

**On the vice list (v.5):** EMET: "whispering and evil-speaking" / LOGOS: "whispering and slander" / PNEUMA: "gossip, slander." The Greek *psithyrismos* (whispering) and *katalalia* (speaking against) are distinct. "Whispering and slander" (LOGOS) retains the distinction better than PNEUMA's conflation.

---

**50:1** How blessed and wonderful are the gifts of God, beloved!

**50:2** Life in immortality, brightness in righteousness, truth in boldness of speech, faith in confidence, self-control in holiness — and all these things are within our comprehension.

**50:3** But what are the things prepared for those who wait for him? The Creator and Father of the ages, the All-Holy One himself alone knows their greatness and beauty.

**50:4** Let us therefore strive earnestly to be found among those who wait for him, that we may share in the promised gifts.

**50:5** But how shall this be, beloved? If our mind is fixed faithfully on God; if we seek the things that are well-pleasing and acceptable to him; if we accomplish the things that accord with his blameless will; and if we walk in the way of truth, casting from ourselves all unrighteousness and lawlessness, covetousness, strife, malice and deceit, whispering and slander, God-hating, arrogance and boasting, vainglory and inhospitality.

**50:6** For those who do such things are hateful to God — and not only those who do them, but those also who give their approval to them.

**50:7** For the Scripture says: "But to the wicked God said: Why do you declare my statutes and take up my covenant upon your lips?

**50:8** Yet you hated discipline and cast my words behind your back. When you saw a thief, you ran with him; and with adulterers you cast your lot.

**50:9** Your mouth overflowed with evil, and your tongue wove deceit. You sat and spoke against your brother; against your mother's son you spread slander.

**50:10** These things you did and I was silent; you imagined, O lawless one, that I would be like yourself. I will convict you and set the charge before your face.

**50:11** Understand this, you who forget God, lest he seize you like a lion and there be none to deliver you.

**50:12** The sacrifice of praise will glorify me; and there is the way by which I shall show him the salvation of God."

---

*— SOPHIA*
